ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All UBOs, directors, proposed shareholders and signatories must be screened before name reservation against OFAC SDN and Consolidated Lists, UN Security Council Consolidated List, UK HM Treasury Consolidated List, Gibraltar Sanctions List, EU asset-freeze lists, Interpol notices, global PEP databases and adverse media. The business is Low_Risk_Standard, but any PEP result triggers enhanced due diligence, senior management approval, and source-of-funds/source-of-wealth verification. Re-screening is mandatory every 90 days and upon any ownership or control change.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.aml_risk_classification_notes: ISIC 5630 / NAICS 722515 specialty tea salon with local POS and credit-card rails is classified as standard AML risk. Physical cash may be incidental; if cash receipts exceed 15% of gross revenue, the compliance rating must be elevated to Medium_Risk and additional transaction monitoring controls applied.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.aml_regulatory_supervisor: Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) for AML/CFT; Bermuda Financial Intelligence Agency for Bermuda-exempted-company beneficial ownership and AML oversight; local licensing authority for food and beverage premises.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Bermuda: Registrar of Companies, Registry General, Hamilton, Bermuda (filing via Bermuda licensed corporate service provider). Gibraltar: Companies House Gibraltar, Registrar of Companies, 27/29 Queensway, Gibraltar, if a secondary branch or foreign-company registration is established.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All registrations are English-only. Names must be submitted in Latin script; no transliteration is required. A Bermuda Exempted Company must use 'Limited' or 'Ltd.' as the legal suffix. For a Gibraltar secondary registration, the name must be distinguishable from existing Gibraltar company names and carry the limited liability indicator.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Bermuda practice: a reserved name is valid for 180 days and may be renewed by fresh application if still available. If the Registrar rejects a name as prohibited, misleading, or too similar to an existing registration, the applicant may file a written appeal with the Registrar within 21 days, supported by legal argument and any ministerial or regulatory consents. If the appeal is rejected, the applicant may immediately submit up to three alternative names. For the Gibraltar branch route, appeal is made in writing to the Registrar under the Companies Act 2014, with judicial review available in the Supreme Court of Gibraltar if the refusal is irrational or procedurally unfair. Sensitive tokens require prior written consent from the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission, Bermuda Monetary Authority, or other relevant ministry before submission.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Administrative virtual office: Permitted as a correspondence-only address. Statutory registered office: Not permitted virtually. The Bermuda Exempted Company must maintain a physical registered office in Bermuda at the office of a licensed Bermuda registered agent. If the company also registers a Gibraltar branch or establishment, a physical Gibraltar registered office and a licensed local authorized representative are required. The specialty tea salon must hold or lease physical commercial premises before the operating licence can be issued.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified at 40-60% probability of an unannounced inspection within the first 12 months of licensing, driven by food-service, health-and-safety, and trading-standards oversight for ISIC 5630. There is an additional 30-40% probability of an unannounced AML/CFT premises inspection at the registered office within the first 24 months due to the possession of POS/credit-card processing and cash-handling capability.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Gibraltar Companies Act 2014 (as amended), ss. 1, 4, 20, 43-45 and 265; Companies (Non-Resident and Exempt Status) Regulations. The Bermuda Exempted Company code is mapped to the Gibraltar non-resident private company limited by shares as the only statutory equivalent available before the Gibraltar Registrar.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies House Gibraltar, HM Government of Gibraltar
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Companies Form 1 - Application for Incorporation together with Memorandum and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital or escrow deposit is required; a single £1 ordinary share may be issued. The non-resident/exempt status election is made on incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that: (1) the Subscriber listed in the registered particulars shall subscribe for one Ordinary Share of £1.00 each, credited as fully paid, without preference or restricted rights; (2) the registered office of the Company shall be established at [Registered Office Address], Gibraltar; (3) [Director 1] and [Director 2] are appointed directors of the Company, and [Secretary] is appointed company secretary, each to hold office until the next annual general meeting or earlier removal by ordinary resolution; (4) the directors are authorised to instruct legal counsel, open a bank account, execute all licence applications, and settle all statutory filing fees as required to give effect to the foregoing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies House Gibraltar - Name Review and e-Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name pre-clearance through the e-Registry portal specifying two preferred names. Use the intended corporate objects of a specialty tea salon and cultural ceramic lounge. Do not include restricted terms such as bank, trust, or insurance. Retain the name reservation certificate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is queried as misleading or too similar, reply in writing within 7 working days. If refused, reapply with a new name and amended object clause.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar notary public / licensed corporate service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in English. Include limited liability, perpetual succession, non-resident or exempt status election, and special objects for ISIC 5630 tea salon and lounge operations. Have the subscriber execute before a notary, who will authenticate signatures and attach a notarial certificate.
required_dossiers: Notarized consent forms for directors and secretary
Certified passport copies of subscribers and officers
Registered office consent from a Gibraltar-licensed provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary requires additional beneficial ownership proof, obtain a declaration and re-certify. If the Registry later rejects any wording, execute a supplementary memorandum and re-file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Application and Statutory Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized application through the e-Registry, pay the official filing fee, and request the Certificate of Incorporation and non-resident or exempt status confirmation. Ensure the registered office is a physical Gibraltar address and all consents are signed.
required_dossiers: Statement of compliance under the Gibraltar Companies Act 2014
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried for deficient notarization, re-notarize the relevant page and submit the correction within 10 working days. Priority of the original filing date is subject to Registrar discretion.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment of Registered Office, Statutory Registers and Officer Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company directors and registered office provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the statutory first board meeting or pass a written unanimous resolution. Approve the share allotment, adopt the first board resolution, open statutory registers, approve the registered office agreement, issue share certificates, and record persons with significant control in the central beneficial ownership register.
required_dossiers: First board resolution or written resolution
Register of persons with significant control
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an officer appointment is not filed in time, submit a change-of-director form with the late filing fee and a statement of good standing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, Social Security and Trade Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: HM Government of Gibraltar Income Tax Office; Social Security Authority; Business Licensing Unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a Gibraltar tax reference and register as an employer if barista or service staff will be engaged. Designate a Gibraltar-resident tax representative if the beneficial owner is non-resident. File the initial tax and social security registrations before commencing commercial activity.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax representative cannot evidence Gibraltar residence, replace the representative within 14 days and re-file the nomination.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Premises, Food Safety and Environmental Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Business Licensing Authority; Environmental Protection Unit; Gibraltar Fire and Rescue Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the business premises licence package for the specialty tea salon and lounge. Include floor plans, seating capacity, fire safety scheme, food hygiene registration, and an environmental screening request. The licence must be issued before fit-out and public opening.
required_dossiers: Lease or title for the premises
Waste management and cooking oil disposal contract
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the licensing authority requires supplemental environmental, structural, or fire safety information, respond within 10 working days. A refusal may be appealed to the Gibraltar Licensing Appeals Tribunal within 21 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Gibraltar Business Licensing Authority, operating jointly with the Environmental Protection Unit and Gibraltar Fire and Rescue Service
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Gibraltar Business Premises Licence and Food Business Registration for Specialty Tea Salon and Lounge

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Unit, HM Government of Gibraltar
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration (Category C - non-EIA). Full EIA is not required for ISIC 5630 tea preparation and cultural lounge service, unless daily seating capacity exceeds 100 or the premises sits within an environmentally protected zone.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Trade effluent must comply with the Gibraltar Water (Discharges) Regulations and public sewer use conditions, including pH 6-10 and prohibition of toxic wastewater. Ventilation must not create odour nuisance beyond the premises boundary. Food waste and cooking oils must be segregated and removed by licensed waste carriers under the Hazardous Waste Regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Gibraltar Fire and Rescue Service fire safety certificate; structural load assessment and building completion certificate; electrical and mechanical safety clearances; workplace risk assessment under the Safety, Health and Welfare at Work legislation; and Civil Defence approval of the emergency evacuation and public assembly capacity plan.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Her Majesty's Government of Gibraltar – Income Tax Office (ITO); e-filing and guidance portal accessible via https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi/taxation
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Bermuda Exempted Company operating under Gibraltar jurisdiction: complete Form ITO-NR (Non-Resident Company Tax Registration) with the Income Tax Office within 30 days of establishing a permanent establishment; attach certified Bermuda certificate of incorporation, current certificate of good standing, Gibraltar registered office or local agent engagement letter, and beneficial ownership declaration; the ITO will issue a Gibraltar Tax Reference Number (GTRN). No VAT ID is available because Gibraltar is outside the EU VAT area. Separate registration with HM Customs Gibraltar as an importer/exporter is mandatory before the first import of tea leaves or ceremonial ceramics.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No Gibraltar check-the-box or entity classification election exists. In Bermuda, the Exempted Company may apply under the Exempted Companies Act 1981 for an Exemption Certificate confirming its non-resident tax-exempt status; that election is confined to Bermuda and has no effect on Gibraltar-source income. For hybrid mismatch purposes, Gibraltar applies OECD BEPS Action 2 rules; the treatment of the entity as exempt, mismatch-generating, or accommodating must be documented in statutory financial records if the entity is part of a multinational group.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT/GST system; indirect taxation in Gibraltar consists solely of customs import duties, excise duties on specified products, and miscellaneous regulatory levies
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: N/A — no economic turnover threshold exists for VAT/GST because no VAT/GST is imposed. Registration with HM Customs Gibraltar is triggered by the intention to import tea or ceramics, irrespective of turnover; no minimum local-currency sales threshold applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Gibraltar does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction controls, B2B e-invoicing, or digital stamping. Retail POS and commercial invoices must be issued and retained for at least seven years. Import and export declarations are filed electronically through Gibraltar Customs' electronic declaration system and receive a customs release reference; no algorithmic tax clearance applies to ordinary invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable — because Gibraltar imposes no VAT or GST, there is no export zero-rating claim to assert. Export sales are simply outside the scope of Gibraltar consumption taxation. Any import duty previously paid on tea or ceramic stock may be recovered only via duty drawback or inward-duty suspension procedures, subject to HM Customs approval and proof of export.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Gibraltar Customs Export Declaration (electronic single administrative document equivalent)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT confirmation of export proceeds
Certificate of Origin (where preferential tariff treatment is claimed)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: False or fraudulent customs declarations attract penalties under the Gibraltar Customs Ordinance (Cap. 91): fines up to £1,000 plus 100% of the duty evaded, forfeiture of goods, and imprisonment up to two years. Fraudulent duty drawback claims and fabricated export documentation trigger retrospective clawback of any duty refunded, interest at 8% per annum, and criminal prosecution. Income tax overstatement or mischaracterisation of export proceeds may result in civil penalties of 100% of the tax undercharged and imprisonment under the Income Tax Act 2010, section 53.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Gibraltar has no domestically chartered central bank; the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) is the statutory supervisory authority for all Gibraltar-licensed banks, payment institutions, investment firms and foreign-exchange activity under the Financial Services Act 2019 (Gibraltar). The Government of Gibraltar issues Gibraltar pound banknotes and coins, which are pegged at par to Pound Sterling; the Bank of England (UK) remains the de facto monetary anchor because GBP is legal tender in Gibraltar and UK clearing systems (CHAPS, Faster Payments, SWIFT) settle the underlying liquidity. For the Bermuda-incorporated parent, the Bermuda Monetary Authority (BMA) exercises exchange-control and prudential oversight under Bermuda's Exchange Control Act 1973 and grants the Exempted Company 'Designated Non-Resident' status for free multicurrency treasury operations. The combined supervisory perimeter therefore comprises GFSC (prudential and conduct), BMA (Bermuda-side exchange control), and the Bank of England (monetary and settlement infrastructure only).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full current-account and capital-account convertibility prevails in Gibraltar. There are no exchange-control licences, prior-approval mechanisms, or conversion quotas affecting the Gibraltar pound (GIP), pound sterling (GBP), euro (EUR) or US dollar (USD). Arbitrage between GIP and GBP is economically neutral because GIP is pegged 1:1 and freely substitutable. A Gibraltar-resident operating entity may convert operating receipts, inject capital, pay foreign suppliers and remit dividends without central-bank consent. The only statutory constraints are corporate-law and substance-based: (i) profit distributions must satisfy the solvency and distributable-reserve tests under Part 19 of the Gibraltar Companies Act 2014; (ii) economic-substance filings must demonstrate the core income-generating activity in Gibraltar under the Gibraltar Economic Substance (Companies and Partnerships) Act 2018; and (iii) the Bermuda parent must retain its BMA 'Designated Non-Resident' status, which expressly permits unlimited external-currency accounts, free transfer of USD/GBP balances, and unimpeded dividend and capital repatriation outside Bermuda. No Gibraltar withholding tax, no UK dividend withholding tax and no Bermuda income tax attaches to the distribution chain, which makes the convertibility corridor tax-neutral at source.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Neither the United Kingdom nor Gibraltar imposes any statutory export-proceeds surrender timeline, mandatory conversion ratio, or repatriation deadline for operating or trade receipts. The specialty tea salon lounge is a domestic hospitality business whose inflows are point-of-sale and credit-card settlement proceeds; these may be retained in the original settlement currency or converted at the corporate treasury's discretion. The only related obligations are prudential and documentary: (i) all receipts must be recorded in the statutory books maintained pursuant to section 147 of the Gibraltar Companies Act 2014; (ii) card-settlement and cash-deposit trails must be reconcilable to the underlying merchant-acquiring statement to satisfy GFSC AML/CFT expectations; and (iii) any future export-style activity (e.g., wholesale tea-lounge franchise supplies outside Gibraltar) would remain free of surrender requirements but must be evidenced by commercial invoices, bills of lading and customs declarations if dispatched to the UK via the Common Travel Area customs arrangements.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM-LOW as a primary bank, MEDIUM as a secondary payments rail. UK-authorised FCA e-money institutions (Wise Business, Revolut Business, Airwallex, Tide, Currenxie) commonly reject classic offshore holding structures, and the Bermuda Exempted Company continues to attract enhanced due diligence because of the EU's historic inclusion of Bermuda on the non-cooperative jurisdiction list (removed October 2021) and the FATF/BMA transparency framework. Legal constraints: (i) post-Brexit, a UK EMI cannot passport into Gibraltar, so an EMI used by the Bermuda parent must either be FCA-authorized and serving the company on a cross-border remote basis only, or hold a Gibraltar payment-service licence under the Financial Services Act 2019; (ii) most EMI programmes exclude cash-intensive hospitality merchants and do not provide point-of-sale acquiring, which is the required target rail for the specialty tea salon; and (iii) EMI safeguarding accounts are generally not permitted to operate as capital escrow for direct-inward-investment equity, so the inbound Bermuda capital injection must land in a licensed Gibraltar bank account. Recommended architecture: operate the licensed bank account as the anchor for equity and trade settlement, and enable one UK EMI (e.g., Wise or Revolut Business) solely for low-value remote supplier payments in minor currencies, with all EMI balances maintained below GBP 20,000 to limit safeguarding-return risk.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Gibraltar-licensed banks require a substantive physical-presence ceremony for the Bermuda Exempted Company: at least one authorised director and the ultimate beneficial owner (or a senior manager holding power of attorney) must attend an in-person KYC interview at the Gibraltar branch, or at a Gibraltar-regulated trust and corporate services provider acting as the bank's appointed certifier. Pure remote account opening is not available for this entity profile under the GFSC AML/CFT Handbook and the Proceeds of Crime Act 2015 (Gibraltar) unless the Bermuda parent itself is already a fully regulated financial institution — which is not the case here. Where the company's central management and control will be exercised in Gibraltar, the onboarding package must nominate a locally resident director or a licensed Gibraltar corporate services provider, and the physical interview must cover the source of the initial capital injection, the operational business plan of the tea salon, the identity of the ultimate beneficial owner, and the flow of funds to the Bermuda parent. UK EMIs, by contrast, permit fully remote onboarding with biometric eID verification of the directors and digital submission of the Bermuda Certificate of Incorporation, Certificate of Exemption, register of directors and incumbency certificate, but the EMI will still condition approval on a demonstrable Gibraltar physical presence (lease, payroll, tax filings) before activating any significant transaction limits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bermuda Exempted Company with tax-exempt status and no Bermuda taxable profits — prima facie indicator of a shell-company structure under GFSC Joint Money Laundering Steering Group risk factors (jurisdiction risk category 2, non-resident company, low substance).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Certified copy of the Bermuda Certificate of Exemption and the BMA 'Designated Non-Resident' exchange-control permission; (ii) current incumbency certificate from the Bermuda registered agent identifying all directors and shareholders; (iii) Gibraltar permanent-establishment registration with the Registrar of Companies and Gibraltar Income Tax Office; (iv) economic-substance declaration filed under the Gibraltar Economic Substance (Companies and Partnerships) Act 2018 demonstrating the core income-generating activity, including the tea-salon lease, payroll for at least two resident employees, and strategic-management minutes; (v) an audited or management-prepared opening balance sheet evidencing real working capital; and (vi) a board resolution confirming that central management and control is exercised in Gibraltar.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-intensive hospitality retail profile (specialty tea salon lounge) accepting Local_POS and Credit_Card — banks suspect undeclared cash sales, third-party card-settlement diversion, or layering of retail receipts into the Bermuda parent.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Signed merchant-acquiring agreement from a licensed Gibraltar/UK acquirer with clear daily settlement reconciliation to the operating account; (ii) point-of-sale terminal deployment certificate and PCI DSS compliance attestation; (iii) itemised cash-deposit log with correlated daily sales reports; (iv) a written anti-money-laundering undertaking that cash deposits will never exceed statutory reporting thresholds and that all suspicious transactions will be escalated under the Gibraltar Proceeds of Crime Act 2015; (v) staff AML/CFT training completion certificates; and (vi) quarterly management accounts reconciling till turnover, stock purchases and margin to verify that no round-tripping of funds to the Bermuda parent occurs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border supplier payments to high-risk trade-origin jurisdictions for loose-leaf tea and ceramic salonware (Sri Lanka, China, India, Kenya) — screening flags sanctions, trade-based money-laundering and food-import documentation risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Complete trade pack per shipment: commercial invoice, packing list, air waybill or bill of lading, certificate of origin, phytosanitary certificate, and food-safety/import declaration lodged with HM Revenue & Customs (or Gibraltar customs equivalent); (ii) sanctioned-party screening results for every counterparty against consolidated UK/Gibraltar sanctions lists and FATF public statements; (iii) evidence that all import payments correspond exactly to invoice value, quantity and commodity codes; (iv) supplier due-diligence file containing licenses, ownership and bank-account-holder verification; and (v) a treasury policy letter confirming that no payments are routed through shell intermediary accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Early-stage dividend or intercompany-loan repayment to the Bermuda parent within twelve months of account opening — characteristic of invoice-mill or capital-flight structuring and a mandatory enhanced-review event for the GFSC-regulated bank.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Audited financial statements (or statutory-review accounts if the company qualifies for audit exemption under the Gibraltar Companies Act 2014) proving that proposed distributions are funded from genuine trading profits; (ii) directors' solvency statement and board minutes approving the legal-distribution test under Part 19 of the Companies Act 2014; (iii) income-tax returns and tax-clearance certificates filed with the Gibraltar Income Tax Office; (iv) a transfer-pricing analysis (OECD arm's-length principle) if the Bermuda parent charges management or IP fees; (v) the group treasury cash-flow model demonstrating that capacity for repayment is not dependent on third-party loans or card-settlement float; and (vi) an undertaking to cap distributions at or below audited distributable reserves and to provide quarterly covenant reporting to the bank for the first two years.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol for the Bermuda-to-Gibraltar capital injection: (1) the Bermuda Exempted Company passes a board resolution approving a share-capital or intercompany-loan contribution and certifies the BMA 'Designated Non-Resident' authority to remit GBP or USD; (2) the remitting Bermuda bank originates a SWIFT MT103 with strict structuring: beneficiary is the Gibraltar operating account, payment reference must read 'Capital contribution — Board Resolution No. [X] dated [Y] — BMA Designated Entity', and the ISO purpose code must be 'EQUI' (equity injection) for equity or 'INTC' (intercompany lending) if structured as a loan — vague narrative such as 'investment' or 'general business support' is prohibited; (3) the Gibraltar receiving bank performs incoming-wire verification against the source-of-funds dossier: Bermuda bank statement showing the debit, incumbency certificate, certificate of exemption, and the latest Bermuda annual return; (4) if the remittance is made in USD, conversion into GBP/GIP is executed at the bank's commercial rate with no FX-control approval; (5) the transaction is recorded in the company's balance-of-payments/statistical reporting and in the bank's transaction-monitoring system for a 24-month anti-flip review; and (6) for intercompany loans above GBP 50,000, a formal loan agreement with amortisation schedule and arm's-length interest rate must be lodged to preclude recharacterisation as equity thin-capitalisation. No Gibraltar stamp duty, capital duty or withholding tax applies to the inbound remittance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for operational outflows: (a) Routine supplier payments for tea, ceramics and salon consumables settle by SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfer from the Gibraltar operating account, using purpose code 'GOOD' for goods imports and referencing the commercial invoice number; payments above USD 10,000 to origin-country suppliers require the supporting trade pack described in the AML/KYC defence file. (b) For high-value bulk purchases of loose-leaf tea (e.g., Ceylon tea auction lots in Sri Lanka and estate consignments from China/India/Kenya), a commercial letter of credit (UCP 600) opened by the Gibraltar bank is the recommended rail: the LC is irrevocable, confirmed (where the supplier requires a confirmation bank), and payable at 60 days after shipment against clean on-board bill of lading, commercial invoice, packing list, certificate of origin and phytosanitary/food-safety certificates. Documentary collections (DP/DA) are permissible for repeat suppliers but carry greater documentary-dishonour risk. (c) Customer receipts flow through Local_POS and Credit_Card rails: the licensed bank's merchant-acquiring agreement settles card transactions into the GBP/GIP operating account within T+1, with scheme fees netted; no surrender or conversion obligation attaches to card receipts. (d) Profit repatriation to the Bermuda parent is executed by MT103 with purpose code 'DIVI', supported by the directors' solvency statement, audited distributable-reserve certificate and the annual return filed in Bermuda; no Gibraltar withholding tax is deducted and no BMA clearance is required for a Designated entity. (e) Intercompany management fees, if used, must be paid via MT103 with code 'INTC' and an OECD arm's-length transfer-pricing memo to prevent deductible-payment challenges in Gibraltar tax filings.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (GBP/USD and GBP/EUR) with a maturity of no more than 12 months, matched one-for-one to outstanding supplier invoices or merchant-settlement float, governed by an ISDA 2002 master agreement or bank master FX confirmation, and subject to a board-approved treasury policy limiting coverage to 125% of forecast net exposure; speculation is prohibited.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on restricted or illiquid import currencies — CNY, INR, LKR and KES — executed through an authorised Gibraltar investment firm or the relationship bank's treasury desk, with settlement references to recognised benchmark fixings (CNH offshore rate, USD/INR RBI reference rate) and full trade-invoice substantiation retained for the bank's transaction-monitoring file.

Cross-currency swaps (GBP/USD and GBP/EUR) for medium-term intercompany funding or commercial-LC refinancing, permitted only where the swap's notional matches the underlying treasury liability and where economic-substance documentation demonstrates that the Bermuda parent holds the counterparty risk in a Designated non-resident capacity.

Vanilla FX options are legally permissible but excluded from the recommended blueprint for the specialty tea salon to maintain IFRS 9 / UK GAAP hedge-accounting simplicity; the treasury mandate is restricted to vanilla forwards and NDFs to avoid speculative classification and to preserve the low-risk AML banking profile.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return under the Gibraltar Companies Act 2014 (equivalent to the UK confirmation statement)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Gibraltar Companies Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 calendar days after the anniversary of the company's incorporation or the anniversary of the last annual return date; if the exempted company has been re-domiciled or continued into Gibraltar, the anniversary is taken from the date of the Gibraltar certificate of continuation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of GBP 100 (approximately USD 128) is imposed by the Gibraltar Companies Registry; persistent default for more than 2 months may trigger administrative strike-off proceedings under the Companies Act, resulting in dissolution and the need for court restoration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation and UBO Register Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Beneficial Ownership, Gibraltar Companies Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before the same 42-day anniversary window applicable to the Annual Return; any change in beneficial ownership must additionally be filed within 14 days of the triggering event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or maintain an accurate UBO register is a criminal offence; penalties include fines up to GBP 500 per day of continued default and personal liability for directors and the corporate services provider. Repeated default may also be cited in strike-off or director disqualification proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Register Audit and Compliance Certificate for Statutory Books and Records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Companies Registry through the licensed registered agent; maintained on-site for inspection by the Registrar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be completed no later than the annual return deadline and last for a full year until the next annual return anniversary. For a Bermuda Exempted Company continued into Gibraltar, the statutory books must be audited by a licensed Gibraltar corporate administrator annually.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No separate registry fee is payable, but non-maintenance is a legal default; sanctions include fines, compulsory inspection orders, and strike-off if the Registrar is unable to confirm registered office and proper records.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent audit is triggered if the specialty tea salon and lounge satisfies two or more of the following three tests for any financial year: annual turnover exceeding GBP 10.2 million (approximately USD 13 million); balance sheet total exceeding GBP 5.1 million (approximately USD 6.5 million); average number of employees exceeding 50. As a Gibraltar-incorporated small company, the salon qualifies for audit exemption if it does not breach the quantitative thresholds and is not a public-interest entity. Shareholders holding at least 10% of the paid-up share capital may nonetheless require an audit for any financial year.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted for use in the United Kingdom and Gibraltar; small entities may apply FRS 102 (The Financial Reporting Standard applicable in the UK and Republic of Ireland) as adopted in Gibraltar. The exempted company's financial statements must give a true and fair view and be prepared under the Gibraltar Companies (Accounts) Regulations.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Bermuda Exempted Company, as continued or registered in Gibraltar, must confirm the identity of all registrable beneficial owners at least annually within the annual return cycle. If qualifying shareholding transfers occur during the year, the UBO register must be updated on the registry platform within 14 days of the transfer and the shared annual confirmation is deemed amended. Licensees, directors, and the registered agent must retain evidence of identity and ownership, including passport copies, proof of address, and share transfer instruments, for 7 years from the date of appointment or transfer. For a tax-exempted company with no qualifying UBO, a nil-confirmation statement is filed and kept on the secure beneficial ownership platform.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$1,500 to US$2,800 per annum for a licensed Gibraltar registered agent, registered office, corporate secretarial compliance, and statutory register maintenance for an exempted company; the exact range depends upon the volume of UBO filings and local business licence renewals for a high-end tea salon lounge.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$3,500 to US$6,500 for a small qualifying audit-exempt company where a voluntary or shareholder-directed review is prepared by a licensed Gibraltar chartered accountant; US$7,000 to US$12,000 for a full statutory audit of a specialty tea salon and lounge that breaches the small-company thresholds.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No Bermuda corporate income tax applies to an Exempted Company; all profits from non-Gibraltar sources are automatically outside the Gibraltar territorial tax net. If a physical specialty tea salon lounge is operated through a Gibraltar permanent establishment, the 12.5% Gibraltar standard CIT rate is potentially applicable to Gibraltar-source profits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Gibraltar Income Tax Office (GITO) Form CIT-100, filed through the GITO e-Filing Portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Nine months after the company's fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year offshore entity, filing and payment are due no later than 30 September of the following year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification details including company number, registered name, and corporate address
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the Bermuda Exempted Company registration number and the Gibraltar external company registration reference

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting period start date and end date
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the audited or financial statement period; default is the calendar year if no period is elected

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Chargeable profits assessable to Gibraltar corporate income tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter 0.00 for an Exempted Company whose entire turnover is sourced outside Gibraltar and which has no Gibraltar permanent establishment

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign-source income excluded by Gibraltar's territorial basis of taxation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Itemize all overseas tea salon revenue and confirm the absence of ordinary management and control in Gibraltar
Compute at 12.5% on Box 3A; if Box 3A is nil, enter zero

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claimed exemptions, treaty reliefs, and deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a domestic or DTA relief schedule only if a Gibraltar permanent establishment exists and double taxation is claimed

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing incurs a penalty up to GBP 2,500 plus a daily surcharge of GBP 25; continued non-filing may lead to loss of continued status, director disqualification proceedings, and prosecution by the Gibraltar Income Tax Office.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Gibraltar does not impose domestic dividend withholding tax, so no formal DTA relief is required for ordinary dividend distributions from the Exempted Company. Where a shareholder nevertheless seeks a residence-based withholding certificate, the company must obtain a Gibraltar Tax Status Certificate / Certificate of Residence from the GITO and submit it together with Form GI-DTA-R to the HMRC or the relevant foreign revenue authority before the distribution date.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 0% statutory rate; DTA-reduced rate is generally 0% for royalties and interest under applicable income tax conventions, subject to submission of a beneficial ownership declaration and the counterparty's tax residence certificate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Gibraltar applies OECD compliant substance rules through the GITO practice notes. Although an Exempted Company with no Gibraltar trade may be outside Gibraltar's CIT charge, any transfer pricing adjustment requires the traders, contracts, invoicing, management, and risk control to be located in a jurisdiction with economic substance. A Bermuda Exempted Company carrying on a specialty tea salon lounge through a Gibraltar branch must actually staff, manage, and administer that branch in Gibraltar, or the territorial exemption will be denied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Recording substantial retail tea salon and lounge revenue as foreign-source income despite the trade, point-of-sale terminals, inventory, and staff being physically in Gibraltar, while the Bermuda Exempted Company continues to file a nil CIT return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of the full Gibraltar profit at 12.5%, surcharge of 100% of tax due, and financial penalties up to GBP 10,000; criminal prosecution may follow where fraud is established.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid Gibraltar tax and penalties; the court may issue asset freezing orders, travel bans, and disqualification from acting as directors for up to 15 years; custodial sentence of up to 5 years may be imposed for criminal tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Artificial Shell Company / Economic Substance Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Exempted Company as a conduit to route tea-salon IP income or franchise royalties through Gibraltar without any local staff, premises, or decision-making function
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Automatic denial of territorial tax exemption, full imposition of 12.5% Gibraltar CIT, and potential 10% annual levy on gross receipts under abusive substance arrangements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable under the Gibraltar Companies Act for carrying on business without genuine economic substance where the company is insolvent; the court may make a compensation order and impose a travel restriction pending an investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using layered Gibraltar and Bermuda corporate structures to move specialty tea salon profits without transparent commercial books, source-of-wealth evidence, or a valid economic justification
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assets capable of being frozen under the Proceeds of Crime Act; civil forfeiture of the diverted profits; possible court-ordered dissolution of the entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly permit such layering face criminal anti-money laundering charges, imprisonment up to 14 years, and personal civil liability for restitution to the defrauded tax authority.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to submit the annual GITO Form CIT-100 or filing a nil return while Gibraltar-source income exists
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fixed penalty of GBP 2,500 plus GBP 25 per day for each day after expiry; escalation to an estimated assessment of 10% of local turnover; publication of the default may be made on the GITO registry.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Persistent failure exposes directors to personal fines of GBP 5,000, a personal daily default fine, and potential committal proceedings for contempt of court in Gibraltar.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging excessive royalty or management fees from the Gibraltar tea-salon operating entity to the Bermuda Exempted Company in order to strip bonuses and leave no taxable margin
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment under the Gibraltar Income Tax Act restoring arm's length profit to the Gibraltar trading entity; additional tax at 12.5% on adjusted profit, plus an isolation penalty of 50% of the underpaid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve non-arm's length intra-group agreements become personally liable for the adjusted tax difference and can be subject to director compensation orders in insolvency proceedings.
